One of the biggest issues is probably that your build is super low tier and also a little underleveled. Quality builds are mostly trash in this game, furthermore the Drangleic Sword got nerfed so its scaling and overall AR aren't great. It's rough that you dumped 15 twinkling into it. For instance the Black Knight Greatsword, one of my favorite weapons, will have over 100 more AR than Drangleic Sword and has its exact same moveset. Also DLC enemies especially in Shulva tend to be difficult to stagger with anything but the 2HR2 combo of normal greatswords.

Pursuer's UGS generally isn't used by most players as it's both outclassed by the regular Greatsword in terms of AR and it needs twinkling. However it's by no means a terrible weapon so you can stick with it if you like, it should be fairly able to stunlock most enemies.

The main thing I would change about your build is to bring your dex down to 18 for the minimum requirements of the PUGS. You only gain something like 15 extra AR on it with 40 dex. With these 22 points you can easily take VIG to 30 and END to to 25, giving you a lot more survivability and extra stamina to work with. You should have Third Dragon Ring, Chloranthy Ring +1, Ring of Blades +1, and then the other ring of your choice.

If you really do like the Drangleic Sword's playstyle and beautiful moveset like I do though, I encourage you to look into turning into a spellblade build as you gain more levels and getting the BKGS. With 40 str, 20 dex, and then like 40 int and 12 faith you will get around 550 AR with it, fantastic damage for how relatively quick it is. This stat allocation also lets you use sorceries and sets you up to use possibly my favorite weapon in the entire series, the Blue Smelter Sword. God damn that thing is fun to wreck enemies with, close to 700 AR and its R2 might be the most damaging single weapon attack in the game.

The big thing that makes the game a lot more manageable for every build is a bow. It lets you snipe enemies from a safe vantage or pull them to safer locations instead of being forced to fight them on their ground, in their formations. Dragonrider Bow is my favorite because it scales with mostly strength and some int while still weighing only 3.0. Just buy like 500 arrows and you're effectively a mage with unlimited long-range soul arrows without even needing to spend any attunement slots.

Final thing I recommend is to check out a source of blunt damage for those real troublesome enemies, preferably in the form of a greathammer. Drakekeeper's is my personal favorite and not too hard to farm, but you can't go wrong with large/great club either unless you're worried about crimes against Fashion Souls. Most of the armored enemies that are causing you trouble take *tremendously* more damage from blunt than they do from slash, plus greathammers have awesome 2HR2s that force knockdown on many enemies. With just a little bit of practice you can chain these together and kill them completely uncontested.

So to sum up, pop a soul vessel, take your dex down to min req, reallocate to VIG/END, grab a bow, grab a greathammer, think about diversifying to hybrid caster in the future. Good luck skeleton

Strength and dexterity can be raised to meet the requirements for the Dragonrider Bow, which provides unlimited soul arrows for ranged attacks. Intelligence should then be raised to 40 for soul spears. Along the way, infusing a weapon like a claymore with magic or using the magic mace from a specific area is an option. Eventually, raising strength to 40 allows access to the Blue Smelter Sword for late-game content. Ultra-class weapons are generally powerful due to their knockdown moves; greathammers like the Large Club are effective, and the Zweihander serves as a less stat-intensive ultra greatsword for mid-game use.

Nah man, sorcery is still good. It's not completely braindead OP like it was in DS1 where you could beat the game in your sleep as a pure mage, which is why you go spellblade and split disciplines. But trying to play DS2 as pure melee is a recipe for pain, there are multiple sections of the game deliberately designed to punish players with one-dimensional melee builds. This game is all about versatility. You want, melee, ranged, and spells to enhance it. You gain levels faster so you have more stats to spread around. You can get to around lvl 180 by the end of NG, maybe even 200 if you're doing a lot of co-op. You will have a much easier time with str+int than just trying to go str, *especially* early on before you have good armor or the more powerful str weapons. In fact since the fire longsword is the best weapon you have access to for a while, you get a double benefit from having sorcery since int also increases the damage of fire weapons in this game.

But overall it's more about being well-rounded than just minmaxing a couple stats, there are advantages to raising almost every stat to at least 20 and you will have the levels to be able to do it. Eventually dark becomes the strongest magic type, but it requires investment jn both int and fth so I typically save that for when I get to NG+ and my character is already well developed.

Also high str is at its most useful later on. As you get into lategame and the DLC areas, a lot of enemies get beefy and extremely resistant to stagger. This is where the forced knockdown moves of ultra-class weapons comes into play. You can basically just chain knockdowns on these enemies to kill them. Earlier on though enemies tend to have less poise and even a medium weapon can stagger and interrupt them with its 2HR2 combo.

In terms of actual combat, Sekiro places a much greater focus on mobility with jumping, sprinting, and grappling. No stamina. The difficulty comes from the timing and flow of these simple concepts creating a larger sum. The other title is more focused on technical aspects over mobility, and is basically a fusion of Souls and Onimusha. Weapons have more special moves to unlock and a huge part of the game is the element of stance changes and cancels. Canceling an attack or switching stances refunds expended stamina, and each stance has different attacks and special moves.
